title: An overlay must not cover the button that toggles it, and the content it covers must be inert
rule: When a button slides a panel, drawer or list in over other content (a narrow-window overlay, a slide-over), keep the toggle button outside the covered area (anchor the overlay below or beside the bar that holds the button, or give the bar a higher stacking level), and make the covered content `inert` while the overlay is open so Tab and clicks cannot reach controls hidden under it. Closing only by Escape is not enough for a mouse user. Test it with a Playwright step that opens the overlay, checks its box does not overlap the toggle, checks the covered region is inert and Tab skips it, and closes it again with a click on the same button.
rationale: E50.3 (#574): below 1100 px the slid-in font list was absolutely positioned over the whole pane, including the pane head with its own Fonts toggle, so a mouse user could not close it and Tab moved focus onto hidden pane-head controls.
